# cdhexmap

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

cdhexmap is a package that provides a shapefile in hexagonal form as inspired by the Daily Kos map style. It also provides descriptive names for each district, as inspired by [Daily Kos](https://www.dailykos.com/stories/2022/8/8/2113098/-The-Daily-Kos-Elections-naming-guide-to-this-decade-s-new-congressional-districts).

## Installation

You can install the development version of cdhexmap from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
remotes::install_github("kuriwaki/cdhexmap")
```

If you have the repository on your computer, you can open the Rstudio Project (.Rproj) and use devtools:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
devtools::load_all()
```

`load_all` is a fast way to get your changes implemented. To fully install the changes installed and working across sessions, you will need to install.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
devtools::install()
```

Read more about the terms and customs for making a R package at <https://r-pkgs.org/>.

## Example

The main output of the package is a dataset, which comes pre-loaded with the package.

```{r example}
library(cdhexmap)
```

The package names the shapefiles by the year of the congress.

|Object | Congress | Years in Session | Year Elected | Year up for Election | 
|-------|----------|-------|---------------|----------|
|`c2005_shp` | 109th | 2005-2006 | 2004 | 2006 |
|`c2007_shp` | 110th | 2007-2008 | 2006 | 2008 |
|`c2009_shp` | 111th | 2009-2010 | 2008 | 2010 |
|`c2011_shp` | 112th | 2011-2012 | 2010 | 2012 |
|`c2013_shp` | 113th | 2013-2014 | 2012 | 2014 | 
|`c2015_shp` | 114th | 2015-2016 | 2014 | 2016 |
|`c2017_shp` | 115th | 2017-2018 | 2016 | 2018 |
|`c2019_shp` | 116th | 2019-2020 | 2018 | 2020 |
|`c2021_shp` | 117th | 2021-2022 | 2020 | 2022 |
|`c2023_shp` | 118th | 2023-2024 | 2022 | 2024 |
|`c2025_shp` | 119th | 2025-2026 | 2024 | 2026 |


Each file is a shapefile:

```{r}
c2009_shp
```

```{r geomsf}
c2009_shp |> 
  ggplot() + geom_sf(fill = "white") + theme_void() +
  geom_sf_text(aes(label = district, geometry = center), size = 1)
```
